newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: U.S. eyes Colombian rebels' drug connection.
newsitem.headline: U.S. eyes Colombian rebels' drug connection.

text.p: The United States is preparing an extensive report on the alleged role of leftist guerrillas in Colombia's drug trade, the U.S. embassy said on Monday.
"We can confirm that the ambassador has asked for an interagency study of the narco-guerrilla connection," an embassy spokesman said, referring to Myles Frechette, the U.S. envoy to Colombia.

He did not elaborate, but a report in weekend editions of El Pais -- the leading daily in Colombia's southwest city of Cali -- said the report would be completed next month and was being drafted by the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, the Defence Department and the State Department.
The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) has been accused for years now of providing protection for rural drug farms and laboratories.

But Colombian military officials led by Army chief Gen. Harold Bedoya have argued in recent months that the FARC has gone beyond protection rackets to become a drug cartel in its own right, rivaling or even surpassing the infamous Cali and Medellin drug organisations.
Bedoya and other officials maintain that it is now impossible to draw the line between counter-insurgency and counter-narcotics operations in Colombia.

Colombian military sources say this could ultimately lead the United States to become directly involved in Colombia's long-running guerrilla war, something that commentators in the Colombian media have warned could lead in turn to the "Vietnamization" of the Andean nation.

A State Department official interviewed by telephone from Washington said on Monday that there was no solid evidence so far to support charges that the FARC or other guerrilla groups had created a "third cartel" in Colombia, rivaling the Cali and Medellin syndicates.

He added, however, that there was "clearly involvement by some guerrilla fronts at various levels of the intricate drug production and trafficking chain in Colombia" and said: "We're very concerned about their growing interest in the drug trade.
